findings.description: The hashability-error code example's comment claimed the error text 'TypeError: unhashable type: \'list\'' for a set-literal construction (`bad = {[1, 2], [3, 4]}`), but Python 3.14 actually raises the more specific 'TypeError: cannot use \'list\' as a set element (unhashable type: \'list\')' for this exact code — the quoted error text was stale relative to the current interpreter.
findings.resolution: Corrected the comment in scripts/build_chapter_11.py to the verified-accurate Python 3.14 error text: "cannot use 'list' as a set element (unhashable type: 'list')".
